aria: Animated recap of the Heat's 128 to 110 home win over the Rockets: Bobby Portis Jr.'s 3-pointer with 2 seconds left in the first quarter that made it 29 to 15, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Giannis Antetokounmpo's 20 points and 13 rebounds, the top scorers, how the Heat won, and the next game against Milwaukee.
notes: Box score from the Heat's 128–110 win over the Houston Rockets at Kaseya Center in Miami on Nov 16, 2026, from the SI.com box score and play-by-play and the Covers.com box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via ABC13 and Yahoo Sports), the South Florida Sun Sentinel (via Yahoo Sports), Rockets Wire (via Yahoo Sports), Hot Hot Hoops and CBS Sports. All 128 Miami points and all 110 Houston points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: 29–15 after one, 62–46 at the half, 101–81 after three. Team totals (field goals 46 of 92 to 38 of 92, threes 18 of 50 to 10 of 36, free throws 18 of 25 to 24 of 30, rebounds 40–52, steals 11–4, blocks 8–2) are from the SI.com box score; points in the paint (54–44) and fast-break points (24–8) are from Covers. Miami never trailed (AP; SI.com). Its biggest lead, 26, came at 126–100 on a Bobby Portis Jr. dunk with 3:42 left (Covers; SI.com play-by-play). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Monday's games.

Houston started 1 for 9 (AP) and cut a 12–2 deficit to 12–10 in the first quarter (SI.com play-by-play; Hot Hot Hoops). The Rockets got within single digits early in the third quarter before Miami pulled away (Rockets Wire; SI.com play-by-play). Giannis Antetokounmpo had 20 points, 13 rebounds, 6 assists and 3 blocks in 28 minutes on 8 of 11 shooting (SI.com; AP); his first basket came with 3:52 left in the first half (Sun Sentinel). Davion Mitchell had 16 points, 10 assists and 4 steals (SI.com; CBS Sports). Klay Thompson made 5 threes (SI.com; AP). Eight Heat players scored in double figures (SI.com box score; Hot Hot Hoops). It was Miami's fifth straight win (AP; Sun Sentinel). Bam Adebayo missed the second half with right hip tightness (AP; Sun Sentinel). Houston, on the second night of a back-to-back, was without Amen Thompson and Marcus Smart (AP). The Heat host Milwaukee, Antetokounmpo's former team, on Wednesday, Nov 18 (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Bobby Portis Jr.'s 3-pointer with 2 seconds left in the first quarter, assisted by Davion Mitchell, that made it 29–15 (SI.com play-by-play; Hot Hot Hoops: "Bobby Portis Jr. would cap off the quarter with a last-second three, putting the Heat up fourteen"). It capped Miami's answer to Houston's 8–0 first-quarter run. It is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Miami Heat or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Portis' measured 6-foot-10½ in shoes and 235 pounds, with his arms scaled to his 7-foot-1½ wingspan, from the 2014 Nike Skills Academy (NBADraft.net), in the Heat's home white with No. 95 (Fox News/OutKick; Larry Brown Sports). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
